Yosemite Valley represents only one percent of the park area. The [Tunnel View](/wiki/Tunnel_View "Tunnel View") gives a view of the valley. [El Capitan](/wiki/El_Capitan "El Capitan") is a prominent granite cliff that looms over the valley, and is a rock climbing favorite because of its sheer size, diverse climbing routes, and year-round accessibility. The park contains dozens [granite domes](/wiki/Granite_Domes_of_Yosemite_National_Park "Granite Domes of Yosemite National Park"), including [Sentinel Dome](/wiki/Sentinel_Dome "Sentinel Dome") and [Half Dome](/wiki/Half_Dome "Half Dome") which rise 3,000 and 4,800 feet (910 and 1,460 m), respectively, above the valley floor.[[90]](#cite_note-90) [Taft Point](/wiki/Taft_Point "Taft Point") provides notable views of the valley floor, 3,500 feet (1,100 m) below.[[91]](#cite_note-91)

The high country of Yosemite contains other important features such as [Tuolumne Meadows](/wiki/Tuolumne_Meadows "Tuolumne Meadows"), [Dana Meadows](/wiki/Dana_Meadows_(California) "Dana Meadows (California)"), the [Clark Range](/wiki/Clark_Range_(California) "Clark Range (California)"), the [Cathedral Range](/wiki/Cathedral_Range "Cathedral Range"), and the [Kuna Crest](/wiki/Kuna_Crest "Kuna Crest"). The [Sierra Crest](/wiki/Sierra_Crest "Sierra Crest") and the [Pacific Crest Trail](/wiki/Pacific_Crest_Trail "Pacific Crest Trail") run through Yosemite. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/66/Neptune_Orbit.gif)](/wiki/File:Neptune_Orbit.gif)

Neptune (red arc) completes one orbit around the Sun (centre) for every 164.79 orbits of Earth. The light blue dot represents Uranus.

The average distance between Neptune and the Sun is 4.5 billion km (about 30.1 [astronomical units](/wiki/Astronomical_unit "Astronomical unit") (AU), the mean distance from the Earth to the Sun), and it completes an orbit on average every 164.79 years, subject to a variability of around ±0.1 years. The perihelion distance is 29.81 AU, and the aphelion distance is 30.33 AU.[[i]](#cite_note-148) Neptune's [orbital eccentricity](/wiki/Orbital_eccentricity "Orbital eccentricity") is only 0.008678, making it the planet in the Solar System with the second most circular orbit after [Venus](/wiki/Venus "Venus").[[140]](#cite_note-149) The orbit of Neptune is [inclined](/wiki/Orbital_inclination "Orbital inclination") 1.77° compared to that of Earth.

On 11 July 2011, Neptune completed its first full [barycentric](/wiki/Barycenter "Barycenter") orbit since its discovery in 1846;[[141]](#cite_note-obsjul711-150) it did not appear at its exact discovery position in the sky because Earth was in a different location in its 365.26-day orbit. Because of the motion of the Sun in relation to the barycentre of the Solar System, on 11 July, Neptune was not at its exact discovery position in relation to the Sun—if the more common [heliocentric coordinate system](/wiki/Solar_coordinate_systems "Solar coordinate systems") is used, the discovery longitude was reached on 12 July 2011.[[13]](#cite_note-fact2-16)[[142]](#cite_note-UT2010-08-151)[[143]](#cite_note-152)[[144]](#cite_note-Horizons2011-153)

In *My Life*, Clinton covered his life chronologically, beginning with his early years in [Hope, Arkansas](/wiki/Hope,_Arkansas "Hope, Arkansas"), and his family's move to [Hot Springs, Arkansas](/wiki/Hot_Springs,_Arkansas "Hot Springs, Arkansas"), where he attended school and learned the [tenor saxophone](/wiki/Tenor_saxophone "Tenor saxophone"). It later had a peripheral role in his political public appearances. He had an early interest in politics, which he pursued in college. He eventually ran for and won the [Governorship](/wiki/Governor_of_Arkansas "Governor of Arkansas") of [Arkansas](/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas"), and later, the [Presidency](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") of the United States. Along the way, Clinton offers anecdotes of ordinary people he had interacted with over the years.

Early in Clinton's life, he recalls listening to his family's stories of others and learning

> that no one is perfect but most people are good; that people can't be judged by their worst or weakest moments; that harsh judgments can make hypocrites of us all; that a lot of life is just showing up and hanging on; that laughter is often the best, and sometimes the only, response to pain.

Following his defeat for second term as governor, Clinton remarks, "the system can only absorb so much change at once; no one can beat all the entrenched interests at the same time; and if people think you've stopped listening, you're sunk."

In a political battle, he said that one should wait for an attack from his opponent, then counterpunch as strong and as fast as possible. Early gaffes in Clinton's political career were a result, he believed, of taking too long to respond to attacks.
